title: The War of the Kings

named.name: Ashteroth-karnaim
named.label: right
named.site: Tell Ashtara and Sheikh Sa'd, southern Syria
named.note: Two neighbouring cities of Bashan; the Rephaites were remembered as giants (Deuteronomy 3:11). Og king of Bashan later reigned at Ashtaroth (Deuteronomy 1:4).

named.name: Ham
named.label: right
named.note: Home of the Zuzites, perhaps the Zamzummites of Deuteronomy 2:20.

named.name: Shaveh-kiriathaim
named.label: right
named.note: "The plain of Kiriathaim," in Moab (Numbers 32:37). The Emites were the earlier people of Moab (Deuteronomy 2:10–11).

named.name: Mount Seir
named.label: right
named.note: The hill country later held by Esau's descendants; the Horites lived here first (Genesis 36:20; Deuteronomy 2:12).

named.name: El-paran
named.label: right
named.site: probably Elath, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba
named.note: "El-paran, which is near the desert": the southernmost point of the campaign, probably later Elath.

named.name: En-mishpat
named.label: left
named.note: "En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh)," "the spring of judgment": the great oasis where Israel later camped for many years (Numbers 20:1; Deuteronomy 1:46).

named.name: Hazazon-tamar
named.label: right
named.site: En-gedi (2 Chronicles 20:2), or Tamar further south
named.note: The Amorites of Hazazon-tamar. 2 Chronicles 20:2 equates it with En-gedi on the Dead Sea; some prefer Tamar (Ein Hatzeva) in the Arabah.

named.name: Valley of Siddim
named.label: right
named.site: the south end of the Dead Sea?
named.note: "The Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea)," "full of tar pits" (14:3, 10): bitumen still rises from the Dead Sea. The text implies the valley later lay under the sea, which suggests its shallow southern basin.

named.name: Mamre
named.label: below
named.note: Abram lived "near the Oaks of Mamre the Amorite," his ally (14:13).

named.name: Dan
named.label: left
named.note: The city was called Laish until the tribe of Dan took it (Judges 18:29); the narrator uses the later name. A mudbrick city gate of the Middle Bronze Age still stands here.

named.name: Hobah
named.label: left
named.note: Not identified. Facing east, "left" is north.

named.name: Salem
named.label: above
named.note: Salem is Jerusalem (Psalm 76:2). Melchizedek, its priest-king, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram (14:18–20).

named.name: Valley of Shaveh
named.label: left
named.note: "The King's Valley" (14:17), where Absalom later set up his pillar (2 Samuel 18:18); Josephus places it near Jerusalem.

moves.text: The four kings march south, defeating the Rephaites, Zuzites and Emites
…and the Horites of Mount Seir, as far as El-paran
They turn back to En-mishpat (Kadesh), the Amalekites and Hazazon-tamar
With the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and Lot, they head home to the north
Abram and his 318 trained men set out from Mamre in pursuit, as far as Dan
A night attack at Dan; Abram routs them and pursues to Hobah, north of Damascus
Abram brings back Lot and the goods; the king of Sodom and Melchizedek meet him at the Valley of Shaveh

symbols.key: Four kings against five in the Valley of Siddim; the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fall into the tar pits
Lot is carried off from Sodom
Abram divides his men and attacks by night
Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram; Abram gives him a tenth

p: Amraphel of Shinar (Babylonia), Arioch of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer of Elam and Tidal "king of Goiim" ("nations"). Older scholars identified Amraphel with Hammurabi; that is now generally given up. Chedorlaomer is a good Elamite name (Kudur-, "servant of," with the goddess Lagamar), Arioch resembles Arriwuk of the Mari texts, and Tidal the Hittite royal name Tudhaliya. Elam really did dominate southern Mesopotamia at times in the early second millennium.

The priest-king of Salem appears only here and in Psalm 110:4, "a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek," which Hebrews 5–7 applies to Jesus. The sages identified him with Shem son of Noah (Nedarim 32b; Targum Pseudo-Jonathan on 14:18). His blessing names God as El Elyon, "God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth," and Abram adopts the title as his own (14:22).
